_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (is_derived = the value itself is derived). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). EFFECTIVE = a value DERIVED to make the explorer reproduce published performance where the prescription is not published. Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text.
_meta.quote_normalization: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) / tag-stripped HTML / string values of ADS JSON / raw repository text; compared case-folded with whitespace collapsed, and again with all whitespace and hyphens removed; primes, curly quotes, dashes, minus, micro/mu (incl. math-italic mu), multiplication sign, tilde operator, <=/>= glyphs and ligatures normalized; line-end hyphenation removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.

m2fs.title: Magellan II (Clay) / M2FS (Michigan/Magellan Fiber System: 256 fibers feeding the twin MSpec spectrographs, f/11 Nasmyth East; HiRes = R2.6 echelle + F2 prism with order-isolating filters, LoRes = plane reflection gratings)
m2fs.recommended_preset: Two M2FS presets plus one optional LoRes preset (table below); IFUM in the next section. Sourced: D = 6.5 m, f/11 Nasmyth East of Clay (M12, W23, LCOM2) with the M2FS wide-field corrector; 150 um fused-silica fibers (NA 0.22) behind 1.2" apertures and ball lenses that image the telescope pupil onto the fiber at f/3.7; f/3.4 +/- 0.1 out of the fibers (M12); 128 fibers per spectrograph in 8 "tetrises" of 16 on a 300 um pitch (M12); six post-fiber slits from 180 to 45 um (B12, J15); two identical quasi-Littrow spectrographs whose singlet/triplet lens group is both collimator and camera: f = 500 mm, f/3.4, 147 mm beam, 1:1 scale (M12 Table 4); HiRes: 200 x 420 mm R2.6 (69 deg) Richardson echelle and a 23.6 deg Schott F2 cross-dispersing prism in double pass, with plane-parallel order-isolating filters after the fiber ends (M12); LoRes: swappable 165 x 220 mm plane reflection gratings (600 l/mm used in HU24, B19, C25); one e2v CCD per spectrograph, 4096 (dispersion, x) x 4112 x 15 um (T17, W23). Entrance (explorer convention "virtual"): F = 3.4 (fiber output = collimator ratio; 500/147 = 3.401 DERIVED), so a 150 um core is 1.400" and a fiber-limited line is 0.866 x 1.400 = 1.212"; a slit narrower than the core enters with the slit width, w/(3.4 x 6500 mm) (95 um = 0.887", 45 um = 0.420"). NOT published: the echelle groove density and the LoRes blaze angles. EFFECTIVE (DERIVED from the arc-line identifications of the MgWide setup, AJPID): at the chip center the four orders 66-69 give m x lambda = 355,789 A (+/-2 A) and lambda/(dlambda/dx) = 156,940 per 15 um pixel, so with f_cam = 500 mm the Littrow angle is theta = 66.99 deg (tan theta = 2.354) and G = 51.74 /mm; the published 69 deg (R2.6, M12) would give 0.0297 A/px instead of the measured 0.0329 A/px at 5156 A, and B16 calls the echelle R2.0 (63.4 deg). The same EFFECTIVE echelle with the sourced F2 prism (23.6 deg, two passes, minimum deviation) reproduces the measured order spacing of the MgWide orders (28.4 / 27.8 / 27.3 px model vs 28.0 / 27.7 / 27.0 px measured, DERIVED). Validate against: R ~ 18,000 with the 180 um slit (JI23; W15, W16 "effective resolution"), R ~ 24,000 in the single-order Mg b setup (W23, P23; slit not stated; 95 um gives 24,800 DERIVED), ~0.065 A per 2x2-binned pixel (W23; 0.0657 DERIVED), 5130-5190 A per single order on binned columns ~300-1400 (W23), 128 spectra per detector in eight groups of 16 (W23), fiber pitch 300 um = 20 px (M12; 19.6-20.3 px measured, DERIVED), and the 47 Tuc Bulge_GC1 order table (J15). Usage: W23 reports 92 M2FS fields for one program, 74 with both spectrographs in the HiRes Mg b setup; configuration statistics across all M2FS programs NOT FOUND.

notes: M2FS fibers are pupil-fed: a ball lens behind each 1.2" aperture images the primary mirror onto the 150 um core at f/3.7, and the fiber delivers f/3.4 to the f/3.4 spectrograph (M12). The explorer's "virtual" convention (core/(F_out x D) = 1.400") therefore maps the core correctly onto the collimator, while the on-sky aperture is 1.2".

The slit mechanism makes M2FS unusual among fiber spectrographs: each tetris carries six slits just after the fiber ends (B12), so the resolving power is set by min(slit, 0.87 x core) and the light loss grows as the slit narrows (B16: "Because the slits are positioned after the fibers we sacrifice roughly 60% of the incident light" with the 45 um slit).

notes: Like the M2FS fibers, the IFUM fibers are pupil-fed: each lenslet images the primary mirror onto one fiber (M22, C25). The explorer's virtual core angle (2.427" for LSB at f/3.4) is therefore larger than the 1.90" spaxel; the spectrograph sees the 260 um core.

IFUM shares MSpec with M2FS, so the M2FS dispersers (HiRes echelle with filters, MedRes echellette, LoRes gratings) can follow any of the three IFUs (TAC26: "generally also available"); the fiber core sets the slit: 75 um (HR) gives R = 36,200 with the echelle, 260 um (LSB) gives R ~ 800-1000 with 600 l/mm (DERIVED, C25).

nObj in the explorer's IFU convention (spaxels per detector): LSB 180 (C25), STD 276 and HR 432 (DERIVED). With 4112 px across the dispersion, 180 LSB fibers of 17.3 px each (260 um) need at least 3120 px, so the LSB pseudo-slit fills ~76% of the detector height (DERIVED, contiguous fibers).

The IFU shoe also carries an 80 um slit for STD and LSB and a 180 um slit for LSB (IFUSHOE), so IFUM, like M2FS, trades light for resolution at the pseudo-slit.
